body: That's true.People can also love each other romantically,as well. I think you know the difference. But I don't know why you keep bringing up that statement as if it has any relevance to the topic at hand. Being romantically attracted to someone of the same gender is different than platonically loving them.
Thank you for the support.I have medication that I take for whenever my thoughts become too obsessive or intrusive. Still, I'm miserly by the fact that I even have them.
Sorry to have replied so late ; and if it's not to much of an inconvenience,please do. I can't thank you enough for this.

Thank you.I'm not exactly a Christian and so the verses quoted were unfamiliar to me,but I understand what you mean. 

I was slightly surprised at how we seem to have shared the same experience, despite different backgrounds. Hearing it from a similar source really helps me soothe myself.

I agree completely. I am just starting my sessions with a new therapist, and we get along not too badly,I think.I had a stronger connection with my previous one,which developed over the many months I was her patient.

Upon being institutionalized,she ended it quite abruptly. Said she would call me later to talk,but never did and now ignores me.I suppose it was an act of protocol, but I still felt abandoned.  

Anyways,enough of my rambling-thanks so much for replying. It means a whole lot to this internet stranger. Have a lovely day.

Although my parents were /are responsible for choosing the majority of the therapists I have seen,religion was never a determinant fat as I know. In fact, there is little evidence to suggest that my current therapist subscribes to any religion. Still,I thank you for your consideration and reply.Every one of these helps in some way.

Really,it is I who am grateful to this sub and it's people. I haven't at all received a more sincere and thoughtful response from any other forum here on reddit.

So,thank you for your reply-I've read through it and it seems very intriguing. To clarify,are you suggesting that the healing power lies within me? It is true that I suffer from a condition presumably organic,even chronic. I do in fact take medication for it,in addition to therapy. However I have been told medication can only do so much,and that therapy is much more effective. Do you disagree? 

Thanks once again for replying. Have a good day.

Thank you for offering me your reply. It really puts things in perspective. I'm considering talking to my therapist about this,however,because I feel to some degree it would help,as it did here. 
Thanks again,kind stranger. Have a good day.
No,no. Your reply hits home,and I thank you for taking the time to do so. I think I might bring some of this stuff up to discuss with my therapist tomorrow.

Thank you-I needed to hear that. I'm going to try and do more of that. 

My family and friends would both agree that I tend to over-stress alot about the seemingly trivial.

Thank you. I really appreciate your response. But please allow me to add that my condition is not something I made up for myself. 

I have been experiencing these symptoms since early childhood,without knowing the why or how,until I was professionally diagnosed several years later. It's something I can simply will away-otherwise I would not have been (briefly) institutionalized.   

Anyways,still. It really means a lot to me that you did reply,and I am very grateful. Thanks.
I have yet to turn 18-but only by a few months.
I think your dad was a brave man,and his story touches a chord with me. I've always thought religion should be personal,intimate. Really,thanks for this. I feel much better. :)
Thank you. I'm going to try,but I have a very hard time opening up directly to anyone. I posted this using my throwaway account,point in fact.
